content:
- Overestimate prices after recent spikes; model tends to overshoot post-peak sentiment (e.g., +0.5–1.0% above true value).
- Underestimate early in the 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or slightly negative; model reacts too slowly to downward signals.
- Overreact to short-term sentiment swings; model amplifies sentiment-driven moves (e.g., +0.3–0.7% over/under when sentiment >0.3).
- Mean-reversion bias: model fails to correct for recent over/underperformance; true values often revert to 10–15-day moving average within 3–5 days.
- Lagged response to sentiment: model delays reaction to sentiment shifts by 2–4 days; correct by adjusting forecast 2–3 days ahead of sentiment change.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts overestimate volatility in high-sentiment periods; reduce forecast spread by 15–20% when sentiment >0.4.
- Avoid “sentiment echo” bias: if sentiment is positive but recent price is flat, model overestimates upside; cap forecast at 1.5x recent high if sentiment >0.4.
